title: Fast developer onboard: pricing & voice playbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working playbook for developer-first messaging specific to the Hosted API: concise value props, three quickstart hooks tailored by persona, and suggested pricing microcopy and examples. Goal: produce ready-to-use lines for docs, signup flows, pricing pages, and sales snippets.

Audience and constraints:
- Primary: engineers and ML/Platform teams evaluating APIs to ship features fast.
- Secondary: product managers and developer advocates who drive adoption.
- Constraint: must be minimal friction (1–2 minute try), show predictable economics, and surface production-readiness signals (SLA, rollouts).

Core positioning pillars (short):
1) Instant to integrate: "Ship a feature in minutes with simple REST/SDKs, sample prompts, and a predictable dev experience."
2) Production economics: "Clear per-token cost, preflight estimates, and committed options to avoid surprise bills."
3) Production-ready defaults: "Built-in routing, fallbacks, and observability so your dev build looks like production from day one."

Three quickstart hooks (copy + why it works):
- Hook A: The 5-minute demo (for product engineers)
  Copy: "Sign up, paste this 3-line cURL, and see live completions in 5 minutes — no infra or provisioning."
  Why: Removes friction, shows tangible output quickly, lowers perceived integration risk.

- Hook B: The integration test (for platform/x-team)
  Copy: "Run a deterministic 100-request test script and get a per-request cost projection and latency histogram."
  Why: Engineers care about predictability. Giving a reproducible experiment helps teams make capacity and cost decisions.

- Hook C: The quality-safety check (for ML/product leads)
  Copy: "Upload a 50-example eval set and get an automated quality report plus rollback suggestions if latency or regressions show up."
  Why: Ties early experimentation to production guardrails and reduces long-term migration friction.

Pricing-language drafts (short microcopy):
- Headline: "Transparent per-token pricing — predictable as you scale."
- Subhead: "Pay-as-you-go for experimentation. Commit for predictable unit costs and reserved capacity when you need SLAs."
- Metered example: "~$0.0008 per token for base generation (varies by model). A 200-token response costs ~ $0.16."
- Commit language: "Reserved plans give 20–40% off unit price and guaranteed throughput. We’ll help size your commit with a free workload assessment."
- Free tier / credit phrasing: "Start free: $150 in credits and a guided quickstart demo to validate in your stack."

Suggested pricing page microcopy variations (short):
- Simple: "Pay for what you use — no hidden fees. Volume discounts and reserved plans available."
- Engineer-forward: "Estimate cost in your CI: run our 100-request load script to see latency and monthly spend projections."
- Enterprise: "Dedicated pools, enterprise SLAs, and private deployments for regulated workloads. Contact sales for custom pricing."

Competitive talking points (concise differentiators vs typical competitors):
- Versus cloud-managed endpoints: emphasize prebuilt batching, KV-caching, and smart routing that reduces token spend by up to X% for multiplexed workloads.
- Versus API-first model providers: emphasize serving runtime + rollout/observability primitives (traces, token-level cost breakdowns).
- Versus self-hosted runtimes: emphasize friction-free hosted experience, pay-as-you-go, and ability to transition to Dedicated/Private without changing code.

Objections + suggested rebuttals (snippets):
- "How do I avoid a surprise bill?" 
  Rebuttal: "We provide estimate runs, budgeting controls, per-route quotas, and opt-in commit plans. Most teams run a 100-request projection in CI to set budgets."

- "Can we get consistent latency at scale?"
  Rebuttal: "Dedicated capacity and autoscaling policies let you set SLOs. Our default routing will fall back to compatible variants without errors if capacity is constrained."

Sample one-liners to reuse in CTAs, hero areas, and emails:
- 1-liner: "Fast inference that scales with predictable costs — built for engineers."
- 15-word pitch: "Plug in a single API, get production-grade latency, cost controls, and observability — ship faster."

Quickstart code snippets (minimal, for hero copy):
- cURL (three lines):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions -H 'Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"rwl-1-large","input":"Summarize the release notes in one sentence."}'

- Python (snippet):
  from redwood import Client
  client = Client(api_key="<API_KEY>")
  resp = client.completions.create(model="rwl-1-large", input="Summarize the release notes in one sentence")
  print(resp.output)

Tone and voice guidance (short):
- Keep it engineer-first: clear, example-driven, and unambiguous about cost/latency.
- Avoid hype; prefer concrete numbers and experimentable assets.
- Signal production-readiness early (SLAs, rollouts, quotas).

Docs & signup flow integration checklist (runbook items):
- Provide a one-click cURL + sandbox key on the signup confirm page.
- Include a 100-request benchmarking script in the quickstart repo and link on the pricing page.
- Add a short (2–3 question) wizard that maps customer workload to recommended model + expected token cost.

Measurement/validation experiments (how to test messaging efficacy):
- A/B test hero line: "Ship in 5 minutes" vs "Estimate your monthly cost in 2 minutes" and measure signups that run the quickstart script.
- Track conversion funnel: signup -> run quickstart -> create API key -> first production request. Use these as leading metrics for GTM.

Next steps (action items):
- [ ] Produce a landing hero + subhead variations and implement A/B tests (owner: Ravi).
- [ ] Add the 100-request benchmark script to quickstarts repo and link from pricing (owner: Lena).
- [ ] Draft a short signup microflow that surfaces cost estimate after sample run (owner: Maya).

Notes / open questions (working):
- Need concrete per-token baseline numbers for each model variant (ask Product).
- How to surface committed pricing estimator in self-serve without triggering sales too early? possible trial: show recommended commit range with "Contact sales for custom quotes" CTA.

Scratchpad (raw lines we can reuse):
- "Try an end-to-end feature in 5 minutes — no infra."
- "Estimate costs in CI with our reproduction script."
- "Reserved capacity for predictable throughput and unit economics."

End of doc — this is a living draft for the go-to-market team.
